corrections.replacement: CloudTraceDatabase(path) still initializes writable by default: use read_only=True. evallab prod status now opens an existing queue strictly read-only; it neither creates nor migrates it and refuses a cloud trace database. Do not substitute it for qa-data.

The default cloud database is ~/.local/state/evallab-prod-live/cloud-trace-db.sqlite. Override it with --cloud-database PATH. EVALLAB_PROD_STATE changes the auxiliary facet, cluster and trace-tool ledger directory, not this default database path.

A successfully parsed call prints one JSON document {ok, data | error, meta}; exit 0 is success and handler refusals/failures exit 2. Argparse usage errors instead print text on stderr and exit 2; --help prints text and exits 0.

The receipt contains admitted, exported, refused and manifest_sha256. Per-run entries have trace_id, blind_id and actor_inputs_available; ATIF uses file and includes steps, evidence_steps_original and evidence_steps_blinded, whereas Harbor and Scout use path and have no step map. Facet selections are suspicion-ranked; explicit ids preserve deduplicated request order. A non-admitted explicit id refuses the entire call before publication.

corrections.description: raw exporter gained strict ids files
corrections.replacement: evallab prod export-runs accepts --trace-ids-file FILE and --strict. Without --strict it can still exit 0 with refused runs; --strict fails before publication when any requested id is unavailable. It has no facet selector. Prefer qa-data export for admission-first facet selection and strict explicit ids.

For a compact single-run lookup use qa-data trace-card RUN_ID [--no-ledgers]: it combines stored detector findings, facet leads, original-step citations, trace flags and playbook cards. This is not the full raw facet record; for that record use traces to obtain task_id, runs --task TASK_ID with sufficient --limit/--budget, then select run_id. runs still has no --ids-only.

qa-data findings requires exactly one selector: --run TRACE_ID or --task TASK_ID. With neither or both it exits 2 with give exactly one of --run or --task. It no longer provides a global per-tool census; do not use bare findings to rederive historical aggregate counts.

corrections.description: both findings modes return grouped object
corrections.replacement: Both findings --run and findings --task return an object with findings grouped by presented run id, counts, coverage, withheld_strings, dedup_capped, omitted and truncated (a minimal summary is possible when the budget cannot fit counts). Each finding retains tool, detector, run_id, flag, evidence_steps, at and summary. --limit defaults to 20 records across groups, independently of the token budget. Detector text is screened; Scout-METR and Docent detector names are not unconditionally replaced with [withheld].

findings reads results-v1.jsonl and laminar-own.jsonl under the selected state's trace-tools directory, plus trace-tools/tt7/docent/arms/*-canonical.json. It deduplicates identical mirrored observations, drops malformed/oversized/unadmitted records and returns admitted per-run coverage; these counts are not raw file line counts.

qa-data history TASK_ID returns the task's non-refuted own issues (including provisional), similar admitted examples and playbook cards. --with-outcomes adds issue trust_tier and available original/repaired reward differential for scoring only; default output omits these outcome fields.

file_count includes withheld files. qa-data task can use CAS-backed packages or resolve a registry-pinned local package from approved locators with digest verification and protected-path filtering. --cloud-database redirects only SQLite, not CAS or package roots: a backup alone is not a self-contained task bundle.

Never read assignments.csv directly in QA audit code, even by selecting safe columns after csv.DictReader: parsing still materializes protected columns. Use CorpusRegistry admission APIs and qa-data split; unavailable ids receive the same refusal and must not be probed for TEST membership. Historical split/cross-key censuses need a separately authorized registry-based aggregate, not the direct CSV snippets below.

qa-data export publishes at most 200 runs per call. --limit, when supplied, must be 1..200; without it a selection exceeding 200 is refused before publication. Narrow the facet filter or provide --limit; --budget only controls the receipt's per-run list, not this hard cap.

corrections.description: cluster facet intersection can silently undercount
corrections.replacement: To count a facet over a cluster, intersect its cloud_run_ids with the complete matching run_id set from runs --facet: raise --limit and --budget until data.truncated and meta.truncated are false. --limit 200 is not guaranteed complete; budget clipping can still occur below that limit. Bind cluster ids to their build and distinguish DB from file membership.

corrections.description: recount does not snapshot auxiliary state with database
corrections.replacement: recount compares the selected read-only cloud database against the auxiliary facets-v1.jsonl selected by EVALLAB_PROD_STATE (default live state). It locks and hashes that file and keeps the latest screened record per run; --cloud-database does not redirect the JSONL. Report both sources and the JSONL digest. Historical JSONL counts differ between these two paragraphs and must remain explicitly dated rather than described as one current census.

corrections.description: help is not sole authority and call count discrepancy
corrections.replacement: qa-data currently registers 14 call types, including trace-card. The help guide still contains stale aggregate-findings and no-single-run-lookup guidance: use subcommand --help for flags and implementation/runtime evidence for behavior. There is no evidence for 17 qa-data call types in this revision; the map's 17 refers to staged corpora, not calls.

corrections.description: task can return file content without --file
corrections.replacement: qa-data task may include prioritized verifier and environment file contents automatically for registry-backed packages, even without --file. --file explicitly requests an allowed relative path and prioritizes it within the budget; without it do not assume a names-only response. Protected solution/scoring-key paths remain withheld. Inspect packages[*].contents and its truncation/omission metadata.

The registry now marks 2 staged corpora as command-level-localization scorable. Enumerate them with the registry scoring.command_level_localization_scorable query instead of assuming there is only one. This is registry metadata growth; keep each corpus's own unit, gold definition, admission and false-alarm basis separate.

corrections.description: manual facet intersection misses sealed-text screening
corrections.replacement: Do not reconstruct the QA-served facet set by taking the last raw JSONL record per run_id and intersecting inventory ids alone. Served facets also screen task ownership and record text for sealed identities; an admitted run's facet can still be withheld. Prefer qa-data runs for served records and qa-data recount for counts, and do not expose raw facet ledgers to QA readers.

At the audit snapshot the registry contains 33 staged corpora, with 31 allowed for local Trace Watcher access and 7 held-access entries. Its false_alarm_basis metadata marks 18 yes, 10 upper_bound and 5 no. These are metadata counts, not independently validated scientific verdicts; enumerate the current registry instead of treating the older 17-corpus table as exhaustive. Historical table rows may remain explicitly dated.
